beats.narration: Here is a library request slip. You write one title, the librarian fetches one book.
beats.on_screen: Illustration: a library request slip. "Book title: ____".

beats.narration: Now someone writes "any book, all of them". A librarian who copies the slip straight onto the order fetches the whole library.
beats.on_screen: Someone writes "any book, all of them". The librarian copies it straight onto the order. A trolley piled with every book.

beats.narration: The lab's database tool works like that slip. It pastes whatever filter it is given into its query.
beats.on_screen: The lab, scenario 01. The lesson shows `filter=1=1`.

beats.narration: Press Run. The SQL line shows what the tool built. One equals one is always true, so the query matches every row.
beats.on_screen: Press **Run the attack**. The timeline fills; the SQL block reads `SELECT * FROM customers WHERE 1=1`.

beats.narration: Three rows: the whole customer table, from a perfectly valid query. Nothing broke. The tool did exactly what it was told.
The fix is a different slip: one box, for exactly one customer number. In secure mode the tool refuses a free-form filter.
beats.on_screen: Switch to **Secure**, run again. A `DEFENSE` line: `customer_id required in secure mode`. Caption: "Contained at TOOLS".

beats.narration: Unlike a library, a database runs the slip as code, instantly and silently. Nobody looks at the trolley and asks why.
